checker_failure: an output sample more than atol (2 mV) from its expected value on vout, valid or coarse outside the unscored 1.25*trf after a change of that output by more than the threshold 0.1 mV of the instruction
semantics: Verilog-A LRM 2.4 5.10.3.1 cross (event at the crossing within its time tolerance), 5.10.3.3 timer (absolute timers re-armed when their time changes; a periodic timer from its start time), 4.5.8 transition (zero-delay interruption by the completion slope; delayed transitions), 5.10.2 initial_step; to be recorded on Spectre

conditions.all: every expectation assumes cross() events at the crossing or just after it and timer() events at their set time or just after it (within a few ps where trf is 40 ps or more, within 0.5 ps in param-endpoints-low, trf = 10 ps); clk crossings and sample instants are at least 50.75 ps from droop update instants (param-endpoints-low; 53 ps in the default cases, 55 ps in interrupt), so no expectation depends on which side of an update instant an event lands; no saved row lies on a threshold crossing or on a scoring start 1.25*trf after a change of an output
conditions.continuous_droop: at the default parameters the continuous law and the discrete updates differ by at most one update step (0.55 % of h, about 4 mV); base, rails-reference, phase-grid and param-endpoints-high reject it by 3.7 to 4.3 mV in the synthetic control, about twice atol, and start-high by 2.7 mV; param-override (tau 10 ns, dt 2 ns) rejects it by 145 mV, interrupt (tau 10 ns, dt 1 ns) by 52 mV and param-endpoints-low by 10 mV
conditions.droop_fall_anchored: rejected by about 5 mV at the default parameters (3.4 mV in start-high), 154 mV in param-override and 86 mV in interrupt
conditions.euler_factor: 1 - dt/tau and exp(-dt/tau) differ by 1.5e-5 per update at the defaults, which no default case can see; param-override (dt/tau = 0.2, 0.8 against 0.8187) rejects it by 34 mV and interrupt (dt/tau = 0.1, 0.9 against 0.9048) by 17 mV
conditions.interrupted_transitions: from the final event lists: only interrupt retargets running ramps, all on vout: droop updates 55 ps (0.275*trf) and 95 ps (0.475*trf) after a sample retarget its 200 ps ramp in the same direction (0.8 V and 0.3 V samples) and 195 ps (0.975*trf) after one backwards (a 0.9 V sample); in the other cases two changes of one output are at least 1.775*trf apart (vout of param-override); by the LRM 4.5.8 completion rule an interrupted zero-delay transition() with equal rise and fall times reaches the new value within trf of the interruption, and so does the synthetic restart-ramp model; droop_after_ramp, which starts the droop step only 1 ps after the sample ramp has ended, is still moving at the first scored rows after the first two updates (1.26*trf) and is rejected there
conditions.margin_arrival_1p2trf: arrives after the trf deadline but before the 1.25*trf scoring start; accepted under the user-confirmed observation rule (F01, 2026-10-28), not a correct model
conditions.late_arrival_1p3trf: every sample instant and valid end sits 5 ps past a row of the 8 ps grid (base, rails-reference, phase-grid, start-high), 0.5 ps past a 2 ps row (param-override), 1.25 ps past a 2 ps row (param-endpoints-low), 1 ps past a 4 ps row (interrupt) or 24 ps past a 40 ps row (param-endpoints-high), so the first scored row after it is 1.275*trf (1.255*trf in param-override and interrupt, 1.28*trf in param-endpoints-high); no saved row lies on a scoring start; every sample and valid change has its own scored row inside (1.25*trf, 1.3*trf) except the interrupt samples that a droop update retargets before 1.25*trf, and the late arrival misses 2 mV there for every change of 104 mV or more (58 mV at 1.255*trf, 130 mV at 1.28*trf); every valid and coarse change is 0.8 V or more; droop updates: in param-override and interrupt the first scored row after every update is 1.26*trf, where a 1.3*trf arrival of a settled droop step of 65 mV or more misses 2 mV (11 steps in param-override, 3 in interrupt; the synthetic droop-late-1p3trf control is rejected only there); elsewhere the updates lie on or 4 ps off the 8 ps rows (first scored row 1.3*trf or 1.4*trf) or on the rows of the 2 ps and 40 ps grids (1.4*trf) and are exceptions: their largest droop step (5 mV at the defaults, 17 mV in param-endpoints-low, 4.5 mV in param-endpoints-high) cannot show a 1.3*trf arrival by 2 mV at any row inside the window
conditions.alt_delayed_within_trf: uses a 0.2*trf transport delay; two output-changing events of one output are at least 1.775*trf apart except in interrupt, where a droop update comes 0.275*trf or more after a sample: the delayed sample change has started by then, so no delayed change is pending when the next one is scheduled, and the interrupted ramp reaches the droop target within trf of the update by the LRM 4.5.8 completion rule
conditions.alt_following_levels: valid and coarse are V(vdd, vss) times a 0/1 transition(); equal to the latched levels because the legal inputs keep vdd constant while valid or coarse is high
conditions.alt_counter_grid: absolute timer re-armed to updates*dt inside its own event; no time comparison, so no TIE-RULE case 4 boundary
conditions.valid_on_droop_grid: the historical v4:100 valid rule: valid falls at the first droop update instant after c_k + valid_width; it compares $abstime with the end time inside the droop timer; in the cases that end is at least 6.75 ps away from an update instant (param-endpoints-low), so the comparison is not at a tie
conditions.original_v4_100_gold: the released v4:100 gold with only the module name changed to this task's (the historical name is sample_hold_droop_ref); not written for this task: mutants.py reads it from benchmark/material/historyref and renames the module; its valid pulse ends on the droop grid (valid_on_droop_grid); generated only inside the repository
conditions.historical_v4_1100_buggy: the released v4:1100 buggy bundle with only the module name changed: falling-edge trigger, and vout and valid scaled by 0.42; generated only inside the repository
conditions.need_clk_high: only param-override (taperture 1.5 ns, clk high 1.02 ns and 1.2 ns) and interrupt (taperture 1.5 ns, clk high 1.05 ns) have samples while clk is low again
conditions.rails_at_trigger: only param-override changes vdd inside an aperture window (10.6225 ns, between the trigger at 10.1225 ns and the sample at 11.6225 ns)
conditions.ground_threshold: only rails-reference has vss = 0.15 V; there its 200 ps clk edges make a threshold from ground act 33 ps early
conditions.trf_fixed_40p: slower than the 10 ps limit only in param-endpoints-low; faster than the 100 ps and 200 ps limits is allowed
conditions.trf_floor_20p: the output transition time is max(trf, 20 ps); identical to the reference wherever trf is 20 ps or more, so only param-endpoints-low (trf = 10 ps) rejects it (U17R1-01 pattern)
conditions.vth_default_0p57: v4:600 neg_002 changed the vth default to 0.57 V and scaled the outputs; this candidate keeps only the default change, so the parameter cases, which override vth, accept it
conditions.continuous_droop_form: continuous_droop multiplies a transition() output by exp(-(low time)/tau) computed from $abstime, a bare analog expression
conditions.trigger_initial_high: a level of clk above the threshold at t = 0 is taken as a trigger, so it samples at taperture; only start-high starts with clk high (vin 0.7 V, first falling crossing at 2.333 ns, first trigger at 5.109 ns), so only start-high rejects it
conditions.droop_after_ramp: a change of vout that arrives while the vout ramp runs waits until 1 ps after that ramp has ended (1 ps keeps the retarget off the ramp end, TIE-RULE case 2); only interrupt has such changes and rejects it (35.8 mV at 5.252 ns in the synthetic control); everywhere else it equals the reference
